newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel super board head calls for more German parts.
newsitem.headline: Opel super board head calls for more German parts.

text.p: The supervisory board chairman at Adam Opel AG's plant in Bochum, Peter Jaszczyk, on Sunday urged German carmakers to buy more components from domestic manufacturers.

This would remove the risk of production stoppages seen during the recent Spanish truckers strike which halted production at many German plants, including the GM unit Opel, Jaszczyk said in Germany's Bild am Sonntag newspaper.
"Because of the tense social situation in Europe at the moment, these strikes can break out at any time," Jaszczyk said.
"For every foreign supplier they use, German manufacturers should also have one domestic supplier. They should build up larger piles of stock," Jaszczyk said.
Short-time work introduced at many German car plants last week badly disadvantaged employees, as they earn only half their usual salary on average during these times.
Last week the overall supervisory board of Volkswagen AG also called for suppliers to be located near to points of production. ((--Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525))
